html:
The Asháninka are an Arawakan people of the eastern slopes of the Andes in central Peru, along the Ene, Tambo, Perené and Pichis rivers and in the Gran Pajonal, with a smaller group in Acre, Brazil. They are the largest Indigenous people of the Peruvian Amazon.

They live in scattered households, grow manioc and other crops in forest gardens, and hunt and fish. Their close relatives include the Ashéninka, the Matsigenka and the Yine.

In 1742 Juan Santos Atahualpa led a rising that drove Franciscan missions and Spanish settlers out of the region for about a century. The rubber boom around 1900 brought slave raids. In the 1980s and 1990s the Shining Path forced many Asháninka into camps and killed thousands, the worst violence any Amazonian people suffered in Peru's internal war.
